request.description: Train a first baseline candidate with the existing PPO configuration, reward, observations, and restricted 14–20 cm target exposure. Preserve its checkpoints and training trajectory as the reference implementation for initial goal-directed development.
request.rationale: There are no completed candidates or development measurements. The consequential unresolved distinction is whether this learned baseline can complete the full uninterrupted hold across the official 6–20 cm annulus, and whether its failures are concentrated in the folded 6–14 cm targets absent from its training exposure or instead reflect broader reach/convergence/hold difficulty. Kinematic reachability is already established under authored limits, so a first closed-loop policy is more decision-relevant than remeasuring geometry. Training the unchanged recipe creates an interpretable baseline artifact and trajectory; subsequent evaluation can select a checkpoint from its exposure/runtime context and inspect first reach, uninterrupted streak, interruptions, and target geometry. A poor result would characterize this recipe/candidate only, not disprove PPO or the omitted-band hypothesis; broad failures would redirect toward overall learning/control diagnosis, while inner-band failures would justify testing coverage next.

request.description: Paired research evaluation of the archived nonterminal checkpoint T1:checkpoint-115712 and terminal checkpoint T1:checkpoint-120832 on the same 160-episode full-annulus panel (seed 4200), retaining episode outcomes and target-stratified reach/hold diagnostics.
request.rationale: T1 used the unchanged PPO recipe and trained only on target radii 14–20 cm. Its logs show high training success near the end, but the 118784 and 117760 timesteps with 97% success are log snapshots, not archived candidates. The nearest available archived nonterminal checkpoint is 115712 (96% training success, mean reward about 115.7); the terminal 120832 checkpoint is also 96% (mean reward about 116.4). Comparing only these actual archived artifacts on identical episode seeds tests candidate-level full-annulus performance without treating the terminal checkpoint as privileged. The recorded per-episode success, radius/angle, first in-tolerance step, longest uninterrupted streak, in-tolerance count and interruptions can distinguish no reach from reach-then-loss and show whether failures concentrate by radius. Any difference is an artifact-level selection result, not evidence that the final PPO updates caused it or that the omitted training band caused a failure. Similar failures across radii would redirect toward broader reach/settling or hold diagnosis; concentration in the omitted inner band would elevate coverage/branch control. This is development evidence, not the protected assessment.

request.description: Run the reusable paired reach-and-hold analysis on both M1 artifacts to quantify how candidate success, sampled reach, incomplete holds and interruptions vary across the inner/outer radius bands and angle quadrants.
request.rationale: The completed M1 result establishes an aggregate candidate comparison (65.625% vs 68.75%; 4 vs 9 discordant wins) but does not establish its mechanism. The M1 artifact inventory confirms that both inputs contain the full 160 per-episode outcomes and diagnostics, while the completed M1 record supplies the same evaluation_semantics identifier (604d52985c97) for both; that identifier is not embedded in the JSON files. The new PI-owned analysis validates episode/seed/target alignment, consumes the M1 record-level semantic identifiers explicitly, and groups outcomes by the training-excluded 6–14 cm radius band versus 14–20 cm and by azimuth quadrant. Its output should distinguish failures without a sampled in-tolerance observation from episodes that sampled the band but did not complete success, while preserving the limits of endpoint-sampled diagnostics. This is candidate-level diagnostic evidence only: inner-band concentration would prioritize testing broader training coverage and folded-target handling; broad no-sample-reach failures would prioritize reach/trajectory and reset/branch mechanics; broad reach-then-failure with interruptions would prioritize convergence/hold behavior. Similar strata across checkpoints would not attribute the aggregate difference to any cause. All results remain a 160-episode research panel, not official performance.

request.reason: On M1's shared 160-episode research panel, this artifact succeeded on 110/160 episodes (68.75%) versus 105/160 (65.625%) for checkpoint 115712, with 9 versus 4 discordant wins (net +5). M2 shows the difference is confined to the <14 cm stratum (9 versus 4 reference/candidate wins); both artifacts have identical 63/67 success in the >=14 cm stratum. The terminal checkpoint is therefore the strongest currently measured candidate, but this is a limited development-panel selection result, not official success or a causal claim about the final training updates.

request.description: Measure the currently best-known candidate T1:checkpoint-120832 on the protected task-reference development panel using its saved controller runtime.
request.rationale: The paired M1/M2 research evaluation shows a large inner-radius deficit and an artifact-level advantage for this candidate, but it ran through the PI-owned research environment. The scientific model leaves protected reset and hold-check cadence unresolved, and the protected evaluator executes each saved candidate's actual runtime. A single task_reference measurement of the strongest evidence-backed artifact directly tests whether the poor research result transfers to the protected development surface before committing the next inquiry to changing training coverage. If task-reference performance is similarly poor, the radius-associated reach gap remains a credible route for inquiry; if materially different, goal review should revise priorities toward reset/runtime/hold-check fidelity and inspect available diagnostics. Neither outcome is official assessment or establishes success under the immutable final panel.

Use scientific work in this session to establish or refine that direction, including building or adapting reusable scientific tools and PI-owned methods where needed.
